abstract: Define $$ P(y)= \frac{\lfloor y\rfloor(\lfloor y\rfloor+1)}{y^3} \{y\}(1-\{y\}),\qquad y\ge1, $$ and $$ T(x)=\sum_{a,b\le\sqrt x}\mu(a)\mu(b)P\!\left(\frac{x}{ab}\right). $$ The Riemann hypothesis is equivalent both to $$ T(x)\ll_\varepsilon x^{1/2+\varepsilon} $$ for every $\varepsilon>0$, and to the corresponding dyadic mean-square bound. The reduction rests on an exact truncation identity for $\mu$ already stated by Helfgott and Thompson (the case $K=2$ of Heath-Brown's identity), applied with a weight whose periodization is the kernel $P$; the new content is this explicit positive kernel, its spectral structure, and the detector certificates. The kernel is entrywise nonnegative and contains no asymptotic remainder. It is nevertheless highly indefinite: along square primorials both inertias grow at least as $\log x/\log\log x$, while on a specific squarefree primorial star the centered kernel has exact inertia $(1,m-2,0)$ (this is not an inertia statement for the whole squarefree support). We construct minimal degree-six, degree-nine, and degree-twelve nonnegative detectors which remove respectively the first one, two, and three odd collective residues. We also give a degree-fifteen detector, minimal in the same endpoint-flat polynomial class, which removes the first four odd collective residues; its positivity is certified by an exact shifted Faulhaber--Bernstein expansion. An analogous degree-eighteen certificate removes the first five odd residues. These are equivalent criteria and structural results, not a proof of RH.
author: lihongmin
change_summary:
1. Attribution: identity (4.1) is now attributed to Helfgott-Thompson [7, Section 2, eq. (2.1)], the K=2 case of Heath-Brown's identity, also obtainable from Vaughan's identity; the proof is kept 'for completeness'; (4.2) is described as its weighted application.
2. Novelty discussion (Section 1) narrowed accordingly: the exact truncation mechanism is background; the claimed contribution is the explicit positive kernel (3.2), its bounded transfer (4.3)-(4.4), the inertia results and the detector certificates. The metadata abstract says the same.
3. P and T are now defined in the manuscript (Section 1) before first use, and recalled at (3.2) and (4.2).
4. Discussion (Section 10): the single-positive-direction assertion is restricted to the squarefree primorial star of Section 6 and explicitly not an inertia theorem for the full squarefree support; noted that the prime-square indices of Section 5 carry zero Möbius coefficients.
5. 'odd-moment constraints' replaced by 'odd-coefficient constraints' (Section 8, two places) and 'higher odd moments' by 'higher odd collective residues' (Section 10); missing math delimiters added around the Mertens equivalence in Section 1; citation [3] attached to Liflandsky in Section 1.
6. Literature-update date: time zone stated (23 October 2026 UTC+8 = 22 October 2026 UTC, before the recorded submission).
7. Author/disclosure line added under the title; supplement link changed to the plain file name. No change to theorems, proofs or the supplement contents.
title: A Positive Reciprocal-Product Criterion for the Riemann Hypothesis
